Advisory (Nonbinding) Vote to Approve Named Executive Officer Compensation (Item 2)
To approve, by nonbinding vote, the compensation of our named executive officers
ü   Our newest directors, Bruce Broussard and Peter Harrison, joined the Board in July 2025 and February 2026, respectively.
ü   Our Chair of the Board is an independent director.
ü   All of our directors are elected annually.
ü   Our directors' skills and areas of expertise are presented in a matrix on page 11.
ü   Directors must receive a majority of the votes cast to be elected in uncontested elections.
ü   We have stock ownership guidelines for directors and senior executives.
ü   We prohibit hedging transactions by directors and colleagues, including senior executives.
ü   Directors and senior executives are prohibited from pledging Company securities as collateral for a loan or otherwise.
Key Executive Compensation Policies and Practices
Our senior executives have a high percentage of variable (''at risk'') pay.
The Compensation Committee has engaged an independent compensation consultant.
We hold an annual nonbinding advisory vote on named executive officer compensation.
Stockholder support for our executive compensation program has generally been strong. Our approval rate was 91% in 2025.
Highlights of Our 2025 Performance and Compensation

We continued our best period of revenue growth in more than two decades, generating $27.0 billion of revenue, an increase of 10% on a GAAP basis compared with 2024. We achieved 4% growth in underlying revenue.
Our GAAP operating income increased by 7% . We grew our adjusted operating income* by 11% and expanded adjusted margin for our 18th consecutive year* .
*   Please see Exhibit A for a reconciliation of our non-GAAP financial measures to GAAP financial measures and related disclosures.
◾  We deployed approximately $850 million of capital over 20 acquisitions and investments, which contributed $255 million in revenue.
*  Please see "Definitions of Financial Performance Measures" on page 48 for information about the calculation of adjusted EPS growth and TSR for our PSU awards.

Nick Studer will assume the role of President and CEO of Marsh Risk , succeeding Martin South. Mr. Studer previously served as the President and Chief Executive Officer of Oliver Wyman and Marsh Management Consulting.
Ted Moynihan was appointed President and Chief Executive Officer of Oliver Wyman and Marsh Management Consulting , succeeding Mr. Studer .
Our Business and Strategy Tie to Our Executive Compensation Program
We continued to evaluate performance in our executive compensation program against the following long-term financial and strategic objectives:
CEO Succession Planning and Succession Planning for Senior Executives
Director Recruitment, Nomination and Succession Planning
Stockholder Recommendations and Nominations for Director Candidates
